tossups.text: Description Acceptable. One attempted performance of this action involved one of Charles Manson's followers named Lynette Fromme at the California State Capitol in 1975. A 1993 gun-control bill was named after James Brady, who was wounded during an attempt to perform this action, after which Alexander Haig claimed "I am in control here." After John Flammah Schrank tried to perform this action, his target opened a campaign speech by noting "it takes more than that to kill a Bull Moose." A 1981 attempt of this action was done to impress Jodie Foster by John Hinckley Jr. For 10 points, many failed attempts have occurred of what action targeting people like Gerald Ford or Ronald Reagan?

In this author's most famous novel, a woman who shelters the protagonist risks jail time by selling a type of beer which has been banned. In middle age, he moved to Jamaica, which is the setting for his novel about a black nationalist party, This Island Now. One of his novels includes the character Tom Lanwood, who is a fictionalized version of George Padmore. That novel, whose title character returns from exile in London to rule an African country, is called A Wreath for Udomo. He also fictionalized the Great Trek in his novel Wild Conquest, and his autobiographical works include Tell Freedom and Return to Goli. In his major work, Paddy O'Shea befriends the protagonist, and they lead a strike together after a fatal mining accident. In that novel, Leah's niece Eliza rejects the protagonist, Xuma, because he is black. For 10 points, name this South African novelist of Mine Boy.

In one myth, this figure wants to switch faces with his wife Rohe because she is beautiful and he is ugly. This figure's father accidentally skipped some incantations during his baptism, leading to his death while trying to gain immortality from the Goddess of the Night. This Kupua took pity on men who were being constrained by the sky and, with his father Ru, pushed it higher. This figure was born prematurely, so his mother wrapped him in hair and threw him into the ocean. After his mother complained that the sun was moving too fast, this god restrained it with either a rope made of his sister's hair or a fish's jaw-bone. This figure wielded Manaiakalani, a fish-hook baited with his wife Hina's hair, which he used to raise the islands of Hawai'i. For 10 points, name this trickster god from Polynesian myth.

A theory in which the universe contains exactly one of these particles was proposed by John Wheeler. The angular momentum of these particles is multiplied by the Lande g-factor to determine their magnetic moment. They're not photons, but in one experiment, diffraction patterns of these particles were observed when they were fired at a nickel target. A photon whose energy is greater than that of the work function can eject one of these particles from a metal surface. The discovery of this particle involved observing the deflection of a cathode ray by J.J. Thomson. For 10 points, name these particles that orbit the nucleus in an atom.

One section of this text speaks of being "forgiving and merciful" to those who "repent" and who "establish prayer." Another verse in that section says to grant protection to those who seek it, but immediately follows the "sword verse." That section begins with a "declaration of dissociation" from those who "had made a treaty among the polytheists," instead of the traditional "bismillah." Someone who has memorized this entire text is called a hafiz. This text is broken up into Suras and serves as the basis for Sharia law. For 10 points, name this sacred text of Islam.

Visitors can listen in on the Assembly Chamber in this city's City Hall while ascending its helical staircase; that hall resembles a misshapen egg. The headquarters for an insurance company in this city has its pipes and staircases on the outside according to a design by Richard Rodgers. Swiss Re commissioned the first ecologically-designed skyscraper in this city, whose cucumber shape earned it the nickname "the Gherkin." Renzo Piano designed a 72-story pyramidal skyscraper in this city called the Shard. Norman Foster's architecture firm is based in this city, home to a column surrounded by four bronze lions and named for Horatio Nelson. For 10 points, name this city, home to such architectural landmarks as Trafalgar Square and Big Ben.

An adaptation of this play which changed the setting to Ballybog was the first stage work by John Banville. A character in this work is alarmed to learn that an official holding a position similar to his in the village of Holla recently tried to hang himself. That character is even more distressed when he remembers that a cat had kittens in an article of his clothing, though Brigitte later shows up with that article. At the beginning of this work, a clerk named Licht is surprised to discover that his employer, a judge in Huisum, has been injured, and was later learn that the injuries were caused when Ruprecht beat Adam, who was trying to seduce Eve, a series of events which led to the title object being rendered unusable. For 10 points, name this 1808 drama, a classic of German comedy written by Heinrich von Kleist.

NOTE TO PLAYERS: The answer to this question is a function like cos x or x+3, but not those ones. This non-zero function of the inradius of a triangle is equal to the sum of this function applied to the three altitudes. The derivative of this function of f(x) is equal to minus the derivative of f divided by f squared. This function of the determinant of a real matrix gives the determinant of its inverse. By definition, cosec x is this function of sin x, and x to the power negative a is this function of x to the power a. The graph of this function is a hyperbola. For 10 points, give this function, also called the reciprocal.
acceptableAnswers: any of these applied to f

tossups.text: An argument over the existence of this concept is central to Gaunilo's "Lost Island" refutation. Bertrand Russell compared believing in this concept to believing in a teapot orbiting between Earth and Mars. This concept is supported by the ontological argument. Aristotle called this concept the "prime mover." Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologica presents "Five Ways" supporting belief in this concept. Friedrich Nietzsche claimed that "[this figure] is dead." For 10 points, name this being that atheists deny the existence of.
acceptableAnswers: the ontological argument for God’s existence
accept synonyms for God such as supreme being

tossups.text: A blue and yellow one of these objects appears in Rembrandt's The Nightwatch behind a girl in yellow, and Jasper Johns painted a "White" one of these. Delacroix painted a woman holding a three-colored one of these in Liberty Leading the People, and a red-and-white striped one with a blue corner is held behind the title general in the patriotic Washington Crossing the Delaware. For 10 points, name these banners that sometimes represent a nation.

At one point in this song, the singer discusses a girl who "enjoys the freedom of a cup of coffee," and a man who "has bulging ideas rather than muscles." This video includes cameos from celebrities such as a television personality known for his famous "lewd dance." In addition to the lewd dance in an elevator, scenes from it include checking out another man's tattoos in a sauna and the singer yelling at a woman's butt while she does yoga. Currently the most liked video on YouTube, for 10 points, name this viral sensation song by PSY who lives his life this way.

At the end of this work, we learn that Kukshina goes to Paris to study architecture and that Sitnikov claims to carry on the central character's cause after he contracts typhus during an autopsy. That character had healed Pavel Petrovich after provoking a duel by kissing the maid Fenecka, who had bore his friend Arkady's half-brother Mitya with her employer Nikolai. The protagonist enjoys dissecting frogs, as he insists that a chemist is more valuable than twenty poets and that the only thing that matters is that two times two equals four. For 10 points, name this work about two generations of Kirsanovs and Bazarovs, a novel about a nihilist by Ivan Turgenev.

According to Eric Foner, this movement was a major reason that homesteading and free labor were adopted into the political platform of the nascent Republican Party. Events associated with this movement came to a head in 1845, when so-called Indians shot a sheriff's deputy named Osman Steele, after which Governor Silas Wright called on the state militia and the Indians were suppressed in the leasehold towns of Delaware, Schoharie, and Columbia counties, ending this movement's armed insurrectionary phase. Nonetheless this movement was successful at the 1845 New York state legislative elections and thereafter passed a state tax on leasehold income. Leaders of this movement in Columbia County hired William Seward to challenge the title to Livingston Manor. For ten points, name this movement, set off when Steven van Rensselaer's will pledged uncollected rents to his creditors.

The author of this story called it a "long metaphor for insomnia." It narrator realizes he needs to retrieve some borrowed books when he receives an urgent telegram about his father's health. The title character learns Latin by reading Pliny's Natural History, and is unimpressed with the feats of Cyrus the Great, Mithridates, and Simonides. The title character of this work is first introduced when the narrator's cousin Bernardo Haedo asks him what time it is. This story's protagonist is crippled when he falls from a horse and is confined to a darkened room until his death at the age of twenty-one. That protagonist tells the narrator of his system of enumeration and of his habit of reconstructing whole days in his mind. For 10 points, name this Borges story about an Argentinean boy with a prodigious memory.

The characteristic feature of these organisms is strongly correlated with differential expression of Bmp4. Many of these organisms belong to the genera Camarhyncus and Geospiza. All of these are found within the family Thraupidae, and were studied by John Gould when their namesake brought them back to England. In the 1980s, Peter and Rosemary Grant observed a shift in characteristics within this group when a drought caused a population's average beak size to increase due to the different ecological niches they occupy. For 10 points, identify these birds that helped to devise their namesake's theory of natural selection and which can be found on the Galapagos Islands.

This deity's control over the wind was represented by a conch shell necklace. After all the humans on Earth were turned into monkeys, this deity destroyed them with a hurricane. This deity was tricked into drunkenly committing incest with their sister and immolated himself in shame. This god journeyed to Mictlan with his brother Xolotl ("show-LOT-ull") to retrieve bones which this god sprinkled with blood to create the first humans. This god sailed off on a raft of snakes but promised to return to his people, which contributed to the myth that Hernán Cortés was mistaken for this god. For 10 points, name this Aztec god who took the form of a feathered serpent.

One side theater in this conflict weakened King Woo's forces enough to allow his overthrow by a general made famous through his exploits in that theater at Yi Song-gye. Some recent scholarship has attributed doctrinal innovations underlying one side's recruiting success to a monk named P'eng Ying-yü, who promoted the merging of Manichaeism with a cult that elevated Han Shantong to divine status. After apparent defeat, Liu Futong's army was supplemented by rebels under Zhu Yuanzhang, resulting in the torching of the capital Dadu and the purging of the Mongols from power in 1368. FTP, name this rebellion by which the Hongwu Emperor overthrew the Yuan dynasty in favor of the Ming.

A poetry collection by this man was published in the U.S. under the title Christmas at Biafra. In one of his novels, Sam has taken power after a military coup but is eventually toppled and executed. "Marriage is a Private Affair" and "Civil Peace" are two short stories by this man who also authored The Sacrificial Egg and Girls at War. Centering on the people of Umuofia, his best known work ends with Okonkwo hanging himself. Author of novels such as Anthills of the Savannah and Arrow of God is, for 10 points, what Nigerian author best known for his Things Fall Apart?

For advancing these devices, John Goodenough won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. A form of these devices using nickel and cadmium contains a polymer separator to function as a salt bridge. In another of these devices, the reduction of an alkali metal uses electrons that travel from a graphite anode ["AN-ohd"]. These devices are commonly of the "lithium-ion" type, which are rechargeable. For 10 points, name these power-storing devices whose types include "9-volt" and "double A."

In peptide bonds, one of these phenomena produces a well-characterized signal designated "NV1." The intensity of these phenomena can be increased by d-p mixing or vibronic coupling. CT complexes can undergo LMCT or MLCT examples of these phenomena. In two types of diagrams depicting these phenomena, lines become curved due to the non-crossing rule. In one set of diagrams depicting the energies of these phenomena, both axes are normalized by the Racah parameter. Examples of this kind of process include intersystem crossing, where a difference in spin multiplicity allows this kind of process to occur in a non-radiative fashion. Sandwiching the electric dipole operator between the initial and final state wavefunctions for this process can be used to derive the fact that the azimuthal quantum number must change by plus or minus one, or this process is said to be "forbidden" according to a selection rule. For 10 points, name this process by which a molecule's electrons change energy levels.

parts.text: Famous peaks in this range include the Matterhorn and Mont Blanc. A hospice in its St. Bernard Pass once rescued travelers lost in this range.
The highest peak in this Russian range is Mt. Narodnaya. The eastern side of these mountains is traditionally considered the boundary between Europe and Asia.
This Central European mountain range is bounded at the south by the Danube River and the Iron Gates. Krakow and Bratislava are located in these mountains.

parts.text: Sponsored by the Safavids, who wanted to spread Sufism into Anatolia, this society rejected orthodox Islam and sported colorful bandanas in support of the shah of Azerbaijan.

The Kyzylbash under Shah Ismail I were subdued in this great battle of 1514 that preceded the sacking of the Safavid capital Tabriz. It led to the Turkish takeover of the Silk Route and the Kurdish principalities.

This sultan was victorious at the Battle of Chaldiran, and would go on to add Egypt, Syria and Mecca to the Ottoman Empire. When he wasn't conquering countries, he found time to play with his son Suleiman the Magnificent.

parts.text: This once-beautiful nymph was transformed into a six-headed monster that lived in a cave opposite a whirlpool, where she ate sailors.
Scylla was turned into a monster by this witch due to her rejection by the sea-god Glaucus. She also turned Odysseus' men into swine.
Most myths said the father of Scylla was this "old man of the sea" who became the father of a bunch of strange offspring with his monstrous sister Ceto.

parts.text: Name this operation which can be defined using Riemann (REE-mahn) sums. This operation is sometimes performed "by parts".
Definite integration finds the value of this quantity under a curve. For a square, this quantity is the square of the sidelength.

The complex integral of an analytic function is zero by a theorem named for this French mathematician. He is the first namesake of an inequality bounding the dot product of two vectors by the product of their magnitudes.

parts.text: Name this Indian religion that seeks to achieve bliss through asceticism.
A goal of Jainism is to achieve this state of enlightenment after death, a distinct concept in Buddhism and Hinduism, after which an arihant achieves moksha or release.
24 of these spiritual leaders in Jainism, including Mahavira, have existed on Earth in the current era.

parts.text: Name this German composer, the third chronologically of Hans von Bülow's "Three Bs", who created a famous lullaby.

Among Brahms' orchestral works is his Violin Concerto in D major, which he dedicated to this friend of his, a violin virtuoso.

parts.text: Identify this novel about a whiskey priest with a child in the Tabasco region of Mexico. Padre José has been forced to marry a woman by the government, to his distress.

Graham Greene also wrote this novel, about the author Bendrix and his lover Sarah. Sarah refuses to divorce her husband Henry, and she breaks off the relationship after a V-1 bomb almost kills Bendrix.
Graham Greene wrote a short story called "Across the Bridge," much like Heinrich Boll, whose "Across the Bridge" begins this collection of "Rubble Literature" short stories.

parts.text: Name this compound which is reacted with terephthalic acid to produce the repeating unit of PET. This compound freezes at minus 12 degrees when pure, but a 60:40 mixture with water freezes at minus 50 degrees.
Ethylene glycol is commonly added to this liquid mixture of hydrocarbons in jet fuel to act as an antifreeze. Less volatile than gasoline, this substance can be used to fuel vehicles and light lamps.

Aircraft with combustion engines instead of jet engines use avgas, which unlike normal motor gasoline contains this compound as an additive. This compound was phased out as an antiknock agent in the 1970s.

parts.text: Name these people who gather for worship in "meeting houses" and seek "the light within."
This sect, founded by Mother Ann Lee, is an offshoot of the Quakers. They are noteworthy for practicing strict celibacy, writing hymns such as "Simple Gifts," and building awesome furniture.
acceptableAnswers: United Society of Believers of Christ’s Second Appearing

This Italian composed the music for Madame Butterfly and Turandot, as well as Tosca.

Rhapsody in Blue was composed by this American composer who also used taxi horns in his American in Paris. Porgy and Bess is an opera written by this composer.

George Gershwin composed an overture named after this country, which served as the origin for the "Rumba" style of music and dance. Guantanamera is an often performed patriotic song from this country with lyrics written by José Martí.

Discussing similar issues to Pater, this Swiss historian pioneered cultural history in his monumental 1860 work The Civilisation of the Renaissance in Italy.

Name this commodore who co-signed the Treaty of Kanagawa, who opened Japan to diplomatic relations and trade with the U.S. by sailing into Tokyo Bay with a forceful display of naval power.

Four years later, the first American consul to Japan coerced the nation into signing this unequal treaty which bears his name. It opened up four more Japanese ports, prohibited the opium trade, and set provisions for future arms trading between the nations.

parts.text: The first avatar, Matsya, is Vishnu in the form of this animal, and Manu builds a ship which was then tied to its great horn in order to survive the Flood.

The second avatar, the tortoise Kurma, had a mountain put on his back, which, along with the serpent Vasuki as a rope,was then used to obtain the elixir of immortality. Unfortunately a deadly poison also came up, which this god swallowed, thus obtaining his blue neck.

Akayev resigned as the first president of this country during the Tulip Revolution. The US formerly operated an air base in this country which was named after its national hero Manas.

The Tulip Revolution escalated after a bomb exploded in the apartment of this Kyrgyz opposition leader. After the bloody Melon Revolution in April 2010, this woman succeeded Kurmanbek Bakiyev to become President of Kyrgyzstan and Central Asia's first female head of state.

Arthur Waley translated Journey to the West into English under this one-word title. Sun Wukong is the king of these animals in the novel.
Journey to the West is one of the "Four Classic Novels" from this Asian country.
